ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.claim: Favours and deprivation test whether people become grateful and fulfill others' rights or grow conceited, and whether they remain content or despair; the peaceful soul succeeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.anchor: He is testing whether blessing someone with favours makes him grateful

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.claim: The successful are content with God's will through prosperity and hardship, fulfilling others' rights when favoured and remaining patient when tried.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.anchor: they showed patience and resolve and expressed contentment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r2.claim: The peaceful soul is the opposite of those who respond to ease with pride and hardship with despair; it stays true in both, gives thanks and helps others in ease, and perseveres in adversity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r2.anchor: If they are blessed with favours, they think that they are being tested whether they show gratitude to the Almighty or not

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r3.claim: Those content with God through comfort and adversity are called contented souls and will dwell in Paradise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p314/r3.anchor: These are the people who will dwell in Paradise.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r1.claim: God's address praises those who passed their worldly trial and remained pleased with Him in every circumstance; their Lord is pleased with them in return.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r1.anchor: they are pleased with Him and He is pleased with them.

QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r17.claim: Being pleased means content with God, and approved means accepted by God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p419/r17.anchor: راضية عن الله ، مرضية من قبل الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r3.claim: “To your Lord” can mean to His appointment; alternatively the Lord is the person rather than the soul, which is summoned back into bodies, and some take the address as a present exhortation to believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r3.anchor: إلى ربك: أي إلى موعد ربك. وقيل: الرب هنا الإنسان دون النفس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r4.claim: The soul is pleased with what it receives and accepted by God; it is told to join the company of righteous servants and enter Paradise with them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p476#2/r4.anchor: راضية بما أوتيته، مرضية عند الله. فادخلي في عبادي: أي في جملة عبادي الصالحين

BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.claim: The natural contrasts prepare for testing through wealth or deprivation and the opposed outcomes of tyrants and the tranquil soul.
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.anchor: أو بالفقر والحرمان، وما يظن معهما من إكرام أو إهانة، ثم التقابل في المصير ما بين عذاب الطاغين المغرورين، ونعيم النفس المطمئنة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r7.claim: Returning to God means entering His nearness and reward; the soul is content with God, and God is pleased with it and makes it content.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p400/r7.anchor: أي: إلى جواره وثوابه وما أعد لعباده في جنته،

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r14.claim: Return to your Lord may mean return to your body at resurrection.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r14.anchor: أحدهما : إلى جسدك عند البعث في القيامة , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r15.speaker: أبو صالح
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r15.claim: It may mean return to your Lord at death in this world.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r15.anchor: الثاني : إلى ربك عند الموت في الدنيا , قاله أبو صالح .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r16.claim: A further possibility is return to your Lord's reward in the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r16.anchor: ويحتمل تأويلا ثالثا : إلى ثواب ربك في الآخرة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r17.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r17.claim: Being pleased and pleasing means that the soul is pleased with God and God is pleased with it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r17.anchor: أحدهما : رضيت عن الله ورضي عنها , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r18.claim: It may mean being pleased with God's reward and God being pleased with the soul's deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r18.anchor: الثاني : رضيت بثواب الله ورضي بعملها , قاله ابن عباس .

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Later additions in 23–24 and 27–30 bring the afterlife dimension into the sura and help decode the enigmatic oath.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: Spätere Zusätze (V. 23.24 und V. 27–30) tragen diese eschatologische Dimension dann auch in die vorliegende Sure ein

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.claim: Verses 23–24 and 27–30 are later insertions that expand the original four-verse eschatological unit and enact the oath's duality as an antithesis.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.anchor: V. 23.24 sind wie V. 27–30 spätere Einschübe (s. o.), die das eschatologische Vierergesätz

TABATABAI:89:23-28/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r8.claim: The address to return spans from revival through settlement in Paradise, or from death to entry into the eternal garden, rather than occurring only after judgment as some say.
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r8.anchor: وليس خطابا واقعا بعد الحساب كما ذكره بعضهم

TABATABAI:89:23-28/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r9.claim: The soul is content because trust in God entails acceptance of His decrees and law; God is pleased when the servant stays within servanthood.
TABATABAI:89:23-28/r9.anchor: وتوصيفها بالراضية لأن اطمئنانها إلى ربها يستلزم رضاها بما قدر وقضى تكوينا أو حكم به تشريعا

THALABI:v10p203/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203/r5.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p203/r5.claim: He says the address to return to God is spoken when the soul leaves this world; entry among the servants and Paradise occurs at Resurrection.
THALABI:v10p203/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح في قوله سبحانه: ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية قال: هذا عند خروجها من الدنيا

THALABI:v10p203/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
THALABI:v10p203/r6.claim: He describes the believing soul's fragrant departure, the heavens opening its gates, angels welcoming it, and its return among believers until the Resurrection; God then expands and illumines its grave.
THALABI:v10p203/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال: إذا توفي العبد المؤمن أرسل الله سبحانه ملكين وأرسل إليه تحفة من الجنة

THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.claim: The believer rests in a spacious grave, lit by Quran or a sunlike light, like a bride asleep until a loved one wakes her; the unbeliever is sent a foul, coarse covering and told to depart to torment.
THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.anchor: ثم يؤمر فيوسع عليه قبره سبعون ذراعا عرضه وسبعون ذراعا طوله وينبت له فيه الريحان

THALABI:v10p203#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203#2/r2.speaker: سعيد عن النبي
THALABI:v10p203#2/r2.claim: When Abu Bakr admired the verse, the Prophet said an angel would say these words to him at death.
THALABI:v10p203#2/r2.anchor: قرأ رجل عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة قال أبو بكر: ما أحسن هذا

THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.claim: At Ibn Abbas's burial, a bird entered his coffin and was not seen leaving; the verse was recited at the grave, though its reciter was unseen.
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: مات ابن عباس بالطائف فجاء طائر لم ير على خلقه

THALABI:v10p203#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة وعطاء والضحاك وعطية العوفي عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p203#2/r4.claim: They say the address comes at resurrection, when souls are told to return to their bodies; Ibn Abbas is also reported to read 'among my servant' in the singular.
THALABI:v10p203#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: إنما يقال ذلك لها عند البعث: ارجعي إلى ربك، أي صاحبك وجسدك

THALABI:v10p204/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p204/r1.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p204/r1.claim: He interprets returning to the Lord as returning to His reward and honor.
THALABI:v10p204/r1.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه ارجعي إلى ثواب ربك وكرامته

THALABI:v10p204/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p204/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v10p204/r2.claim: He says 'your Lord' refers to your peers among God's righteous servants.
THALABI:v10p204/r2.anchor: ابن كيسان: ارجعي إلى ربك أي أمثالك من عباد ربك الصالحين

THALABI:v10p204/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p204/r3.speaker: أهل الإشارة
THALABI:v10p204/r3.claim: They address the soul settled in worldly life and call it to leave it for God and the afterlife; it is content with God and accepted by Him.
THALABI:v10p204/r3.anchor: يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة إلى الدنيا ارجعي إلى الله بتركها والرجوع إلى الله هو سلوك سبيل الآخرة

BURSEVI:v10p334/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p334/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p334/r1.claim: A soul stabilized in spiritual ascent is protected from reverting to natural and human traits and from descending to the commanding self.
BURSEVI:v10p334/r1.anchor: فمن كان متمكنا في مقام الترقي تخلص من التنزل إلى مقام النفس الأمارة

BURSEVI:v10p334/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p334/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p334/r5.claim: Returning to the Lord means reaching the promised honor and nearness; this figurative destination defeats corporealists' argument and indicates the spirit was created first.
BURSEVI:v10p334/r5.anchor: أي إلى ما وعد لك من الكرامة والزلفى فكونه تعالى منتهى الغاية إنما هو بهذا الاعتبار

BURSEVI:v10p334/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p334/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p334/r6.claim: The soul is pleased with its enduring bliss and accepted by God.

BURSEVI:v10p334/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p334/r13.speaker: بعض أهل الإشارة
BURSEVI:v10p334/r13.claim: The soul settled in worldly life is told to return to God by abandoning it and following the path of the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v10p334/r13.anchor: وقال بعض أهل الإشارة يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة إلى الدنيا ارجعي إلى الله بتركها

QASHANI:89:27-30/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:89:27-30/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:89:27-30/r2.claim: After completing the attributes, the soul returns to the essence in contentment rather than stopping at the attributes; contentment with God follows God’s contentment with the soul.
QASHANI:89:27-30/r2.anchor: إذا تم لك كمال الصفات فلا تسكني إليه وارجعي إلى الذات في حال الرضا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r1.claim: When Abu Bakr admired the verse, the Prophet told him that these words would be said to him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية قال : نزلت وابو بكر جالس

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r2.claim: A second report places Abu Bakr reading the verses to the Prophet, who says an angel will say this to him at death.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : قرات عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr describes a river from the Throne's base that grows every creature; on resurrection souls fly and are commanded to enter bodies, which he links to the command to return to God.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال : يسيل واد من اصل العرش فتنبت فيه كل دابة على وجه الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the soul is pleased by its promised reward and approved through its deeds; entering among God's servants means entering among the believers.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : ارجعي إلى ربك راضية قال : بما اعطيت من الثواب مرضية عنها بعلمها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says that when God takes a believer, the soul and God are mutually pleased; He then takes it into Paradise among His righteous servants.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله : يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة الاية قال : ان الله اذا اراد قبض عبده المؤمن اطمانت النفس اليه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.claim: Abu Salih says return to God is the soul's departure from the world at death; on Resurrection it is told to enter among God's servants and into Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله : ارجعي إلى ربك قال : هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the soul receives the good news of Paradise at death, resurrection, and the gathering.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم رضي الله عنه يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة الاية قال : بشرت بالجنة عند الموت وعند البعث ويوم الجمع

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr recounts that after Ibn Abbas died at Taif, an unseen bird entered his bier and did not emerge; the tranquil-soul verses were heard recited at his grave.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : مات ابن عباس بالطائف ، فجاء طير لم ير على خلقه ، فدخل نعشه ثم لم ير خارجا منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.claim: The passage ends the warnings with glad tidings for believers guided by the Quran, following the Quran's pattern of joining promise to warning to encourage good and deter evil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.anchor: ختم الكلام بالبشارة للمؤمنين الذين تذكروا بالقرآن واتبعوا هديه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r4.claim: Because these verses follow the preceding passage in recitation and the codex, their original sequence likely reflects one revelation; the address is then spoken in the afterlife as an answer to the earth's crushing, with the intervening material parenthetical.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r4.anchor: فهذا قول يصدر يوم القيامة من جانب القدس من كلام الله تعالى أو من كلام الملائكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r5.claim: If God speaks, rabbiki replaces an implicit pronoun and expresses closeness and honor; if angels speak, it is ordinary wording, and God takes up their address by commanding the soul to enter among His servants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r5.anchor: فإن كان من كلام الله تعالى كان قوله : { إلى ربك } إظهارا في مقام الإضمار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r6.claim: Returning to God is a metaphor for dwelling in Paradise as God's honored home, like a guest's residence; the soul earned it through the divine promise to reward good works.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r6.anchor: والرجوع إلى الله مستعار للكون في نعيم الجنة التي هي دار الكرامة عند الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r7.claim: The return is a special homecoming to Paradise, not an unrestricted description of entry into the afterlife.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r7.anchor: وهذا الرجوع خاص غير مطلق الحلول في الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.claim: Alternatively, the address may begin a new passage, prompted by the mention of punishment for the polytheist, and God may be speaking directly to the believers' reassured souls.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الآية استئنافا ابتدائيا جرى على مناسبة ذكر عذاب الإنسان المشرك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r2.claim: The imperative to return is a promise qualified by the two following states, satisfied and approved; the return is metaphorical in this interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r2.anchor: والأمر في { ارجعي إلى ربك } مراد منه تقييده بالحالين بعده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the verse was revealed concerning ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān after he donated the well of Rumah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r4.anchor: فعن الضحاك : أنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان لما تصدق ببئر رومة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r5.speaker: بريدة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r5.claim: Buraydah says the verse was revealed about Ḥamzah after his death as a martyr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r5.anchor: وعن بريدة : أنها نزلت في حمزة حين قتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r6.claim: Another reported view applies the verse to Khubayb ibn ʿAdī when the Meccans crucified him; these specific occasions imply a Medinan revelation, against the agreed Meccan classification except for a report from al-Dānī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r6.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في خبيب بن عدي لما صلبه أهل مكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r7.claim: If the verse is Medinan, it is separate from the preceding passage and was placed here by instruction or revealed afterward because of thematic affinity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r7.anchor: وهي على هذا منفصلة عما قبلها كتبت هنا بتوقيف خاص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن حارثة وأبي بن كعب وابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r8.claim: These authorities say the words are spoken at resurrection as spirits return to bodies; on this view the passage connects to the earth being crushed, and the return is literal, with the body as the soul's Lord or owner.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وزيد بن حارثة وأبي بن كعب وابنن مسعود : أن هذا يقال عند البعث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r9.speaker: زيد بن حارثة وأبو صالح
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Ḥārithah and Abū Ṣāliḥ say the address is given to the soul at death; Zayd specifically says the believer's soul is thereby promised Paradise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r9.anchor: وعن زيد بن حارثة وأبي صالح : يقال هذا للنفس عند الموت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that after a man recited the verse before the Prophet and Abū Bakr praised it, the Prophet said an angel would say it to Abū Bakr at death; no grading is stated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r10.anchor: وقد روى الطبري عن سعيد بن جبير قال : قرأ رجل عند رسول الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r1.claim: The return can be understood literally or metaphorically according to the interpretations already discussed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r1.anchor: والرجوع يحتمل الحقيقة والمجاز كما علمت من الوجوه المتقدمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r2.claim: Rāḍiyah describes a soul satisfied with its bestowed honor, indirectly expressing that it receives everything it desires.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r2.anchor: من كرامة وهو كناية عن إعطائها كل ما تطمح إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r3.claim: Marḍiyyah is a passive participle originally meaning approved by God; deletion of the preposition makes it the grammatical subject, and the wording implies further gifts beyond what satisfied the soul.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r3.anchor: فوقع فيه الحذف والإيصال فصار نائب فاعل بدون حرف الجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r8.claim: The first-person attribution to Paradise makes the shift from God's mention in the third person aesthetically apt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r8.anchor: وهذه الإضافة هي مما يزيد الالتفات إلى ضمير التكلم حسنا

TUSTARI:89:28/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:89:28/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:89:28/r1.claim: The soul returns to God by the afterlife's path, content with God through God and approved because it rests in God.
TUSTARI:89:28/r1.anchor: بطريق الآخرة { راضية } [28] عن الله بالله { مرضية } [28] عنها لسكونها إلى الله عز وجل.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r1.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r1.claim: One interpretation of returning to the Lord means returning to the person whose body the soul had inhabited.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r1.anchor: أحدها ارجعي إلى صاحبك الذي كنت في جسده وهذا المعنى في رواية العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r2.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says the soul returns to its Lord after death in this world.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r2.anchor: والثاني ارجعي إلى ربك بعد الموت في الدنيا قاله أبو صالح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it means to return to the Lord's reward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r3.anchor: والثالث ارجعي إلى ثواب ربك قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r4.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r4.claim: Al-Māwardī transmits an address to the soul content with worldly life: return to God by leaving the world.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p124/r4.anchor: والرابع يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة [ إلى الدنيا ] ارجعي إلى الله تعالى بتركها

FARRA:v3p262/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p262/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p262/r2.claim: When believers receive their books in their right hands, angels tell them to return to the reward God has prepared.
FARRA:v3p262/r2.anchor:
تقول لهم الملائكة إذا أعطوا كتبهم
بأيمانهم «ارجعي إلى ربك» إلى ما أعد الله لك من الثواب.

FARRA:v3p262/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p262/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p262/r3.claim: Alternatively, the command means returning from worldly life to this destination; an imperative can function as a statement, “you are pleased and pleasing.”
FARRA:v3p262/r3.anchor: وقد يكون أن يقولوا لهم هذا القول ينوون: ارجعوا من الدنيا إلى هذا المرجع.

FARRA:v3p262/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p262/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p262/r4.claim: The imperative can be a discourse filler when the addressee already belongs to a class, as when one says “be Tamimi or Qaysi” to a Muḍari.
FARRA:v3p262/r4.anchor:
فيقول: مضرى.
فتقول: كن تميميا، أو قيسيا. أي: أنت من أحد هذين.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r3.claim: The address may come at death, resurrection, or entry into Paradise, meaning return to the reward promised by the Lord.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r3.anchor: إما عند الموت . وإما عند البعث ، وإما عند دخول الجنة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r4.claim: The soul is content with what it received and approved by God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p755#2/r4.anchor: راضية } بما أوتيت { مرضية } عند الله

MUQATIL:89:27-30/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r2.claim: The soul returns satisfied with its deeds and approved because of the goodness and recompense God grants it.
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r2.anchor: لعملك { مرضية } [آية: 28] بما أعطاك الله عز وجل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#2/r1.claim: “Return to your Lord” can mean return to His promise or reward; the soul is pleased with what God gives and accepted by God for what it has done.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ ارجعي إلى ﴾ موعد ﴿ ربك ﴾ أو ثواب ربك

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r1.claim: Said ibn Jubayr reports that a strange bird entered Ibn Abbas’s coffin at his death in Taif and was never seen leaving; the verse was recited at his grave by an unknown reciter.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r1.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: مات ابن عباس بالطائف، فجاء طائر لم ير على خلقته طائر قط، فدخل نعشه

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r4.claim: They take “return to your Lord” as returning to one’s companion, the body.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r4.anchor: معنى { إلى ربك } أي إلى صاحبك وجسدك قاله ابن عباس وعكرمة وعطاء

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r5.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers “your companion/body,” supported by Ibn Abbas’s singular reading “enter My servant”; souls will return to bodies at resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r5.anchor: واختاره الطبري ودليله قراءة ابن عباس «فادخلي في عبدي» على التوحيد

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r6.claim: Ibn Masud reads “into the body of My servant.”

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r7.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the return as reaching the Lord’s reward and honor.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: ارجعي إلى ثواب ربك وكرامته

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r8.claim: Abu Salih says the soul returns to God at death.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r8.anchor: وقال أبو صالح: المعنى: ارجعي إلى الله. وهذا عند الموت

NAHHAS:v5p225/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
NAHHAS:v5p225/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr takes irjiʿī as a return to the body, so the soul is addressed.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r3.anchor: في معناه قولان قال سعيد بن جبير إلى جسدك فالمعنى على هذا أن النفس خوطبت

NAHHAS:v5p225/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r4.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v5p225/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes the return as to God, so the human being is addressed.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r4.anchor: قال الضحاك إلى الله فالمعنى على هذا أن المخاطبة للإنسان

NAHHAS:v5p225/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p225/r5.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p225/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ holds that angels say this to people when they receive their records in their right hands: return to your Lord's reward.
NAHHAS:v5p225/r5.anchor: وإليه يذهب الفراء وإلى أن المعنى أن الملائكة تقول لهم إذا أعطوا كتبهم بأيمانهم

QUTB-ZILAL:89:28/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:28/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:28/r1.claim: The soul returns to its source after earthly estrangement, reunited with its Lord in a tone of tenderness, contentment, and divine acceptance.
QUTB-ZILAL:89:28/r1.anchor: ارجعي إلى مصدرك بعد غربة الأرض وفرقة المهد

RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r11.claim: Razi says this account is useful only to someone advanced in divine thought or spiritual detachment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p160/r11.anchor: وهذا كلام لا ينتفع الإنسان به إلا إذا كان كاملا في القوة الفكرية الإلهية أو في التجريد والتفريد

RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r7.claim: On the immaterial view, the soul's return and coming mean managing the body and ceasing that management; on the subtle-body view, they are literal.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161/r7.anchor: وعلى التقدير الأول يكون وصفها بالمجيء والرجوع بمعنى التدبير وتركه ، وعلى التقدير الثاني يكون ذلك الوصف حقيقا

RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r1.claim: Some ancients infer from “return to your Lord” that souls existed before bodily life and were therefore eternal.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r1.anchor: من القدماء من زعم أن النفوس أزلية ، واحتجوا بهذه الآية وهي قوله : { ارجعى إلى ربك

RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r2.claim: If the address occurs at death, it supports souls preceding bodies, although precedence does not prove eternity.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r2.anchor: أنه إنما يوجد عند الموت ، وههنا تقوى حجة القائلين بتقدم الأرواح على الأجساد

RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r3.claim: If it occurs at resurrection, “return” means returning to God's reward and re-entering the body from which the soul departed.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r3.anchor: أنه إنما يوجد عند البعث والقيامة ، والمعنى : ارجعي إلى ثواب ربك ، فادخلي في عبادي

RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r4.claim: Corporealists appeal to “to your Lord” as evidence of direction; Razi glosses it as God's judgment, reward, or grace.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r4.anchor: المجسمة تمسكوا بقوله : { إلى ربك } وكلمة إلى لانتهاء الغاية وجوابه : إلى حكم ربك

RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r5.claim: Razi's rational account has the intellect ascend from contingent beings and causes to the Necessary Existent, the terminus of all ends.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r5.anchor: القوة العقلية بسيرها العقلي تترقى من موجود إلى موجود آخر ، ومن سبب إلى سبب

RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r6.claim: “Content and accepted” means pleased with reward and accepted by God for worldly deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r6.anchor: قوله تعالى : { راضية مرضية } فالمعنى راضية بالثواب مرضية عنك في الأعمال التي عملتها في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r7.claim: A report says that after a man recited these verses, Abū Bakr praised them and the Prophet said an angel would say them to him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p161#2/r7.anchor: فقال أبو بكر : ما أحسن هذاا فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( أما إن الملك سيقولها لك

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r8.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r8.claim: The soul's return to its Lord may imply that it was with its Lord in the Garden before creation.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r8.anchor: That the soul returns to its Lord is understood to imply that it was with its Lord in the Garden before creation

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r9.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r9.claim: Many interpret content and contenting as satisfied with God's reward and pleasing to God for having done good deeds.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r9.anchor: Many interpret this verse to mean content with the reward of God and contenting to God for having performed good deeds

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r10.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r10.claim: Others understand the phrase to mean accepting everything God has decreed.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r10.anchor: Others understand it as an indication that one is content with everything that God has decreed

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r11.speaker: Aj, K
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r11.claim: Some see return to the Divine Essence in complete contentment; content and contenting may express two levels, through God and before God.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r11.anchor: Still others take it as an indication that the soul returns to the Divine Essence in a state of complete contentment

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r12.speaker: K
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r12.claim: Some stress that God must be content with souls before they can be content with Him.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r12.anchor: Some emphasize that there can be no contentment with God until God is content with souls

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r13.speaker: Qu
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r13.claim: Contentment is described as a foremost virtue, the greatest gate of God and the paradise of this world.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r13.anchor: Contentment is seen by some as one of the most important virtues; it has been described as “the greatest gate of God and the paradise of this world”

TAB:89:27/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r7.speaker: سعيد
TAB:89:27/r7.claim: After the verse was recited before the Prophet and Abū Bakr praised it, the Prophet said the angel would say it to Abū Bakr at death.
TAB:89:27/r7.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  «أما إنّ المَلَكَ سَيَقُولُهَا لك عِنْدَ المَوْتِ »

TAB:89:27/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB:89:27/r8.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ places the call to return at death but says the command to enter among God's servants belongs to the Resurrection.
TAB:89:27/r8.anchor: عن أبي صالح ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  هذا عند الموت فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال هذا يوم القيامة .

TAB:89:27/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r9.speaker: أبو أسامة بن زيد عن أبيه
TAB:89:27/r9.claim: A report says the tranquil soul is promised the Garden at death, on the Day of Gathering, and at resurrection.
TAB:89:27/r9.anchor: عن أُسامة بن زيد ،   عن أبيه ،   في قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ قال :  بُشّرت بالجنة

TAB:89:29/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:29/r1.claim: One view says the angels call the believer's soul at resurrection to return to its body; Ibn ʿAbbās says tranquil souls return to bodies on that day.
TAB:89:29/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  تردّ الأرواح

TAB:89:29/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:89:29/r3.claim: ʿIkrima explains the return to the Lord as a return to the body.
TAB:89:29/r3.anchor: عن عكرِمة في هذه الاَية :  ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً إلى الجسد .

TAB:89:29/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB:89:29/r4.claim: Another view places the call to return at death, while the entry among God's servants is at resurrection.
TAB:89:29/r4.anchor: عن أبي صالح ارْجِعي إلَى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  هذا عند الموت فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  هذا يوم القيامة .

TAB:89:29/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r5.speaker: author
TAB:89:29/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the resurrection interpretation because the following words tell the soul to enter among God's servants and into His Garden.
TAB:89:29/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب القول الذي ذكرناه عن ابن عباس والضحاك ،   أن ذلك إنما يقال لهم

TAB:89:29/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r9.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة
TAB:89:29/r9.claim: A Kufan grammarian reads the address as a command to the believing soul at judgment to return to its prepared reward; since it has arrived, the command can function as a statement that it is pleased and approved.
TAB:89:29/r9.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة يتأوّل ذلك يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ بالإيمان ،   والمصدّقة بالثواب والبعث ارجعي

TAB:89:30/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:30/r1.claim: One view says the angels call the believer's soul at resurrection to return to its body; Ibn ʿAbbās says tranquil souls return to bodies on that day.
TAB:89:30/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  تردّ الأرواح

TAB:89:30/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:89:30/r3.claim: ʿIkrima explains the return to the Lord as a return to the body.
TAB:89:30/r3.anchor: عن عكرِمة في هذه الاَية :  ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً إلى الجسد .

TAB:89:30/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB:89:30/r4.claim: Another view places the call to return at death, while the entry among God's servants is at resurrection.
TAB:89:30/r4.anchor: عن أبي صالح ارْجِعي إلَى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  هذا عند الموت فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  هذا يوم القيامة .

TAB:89:30/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r5.speaker: author
TAB:89:30/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the resurrection interpretation because the following words tell the soul to enter among God's servants and into His Garden.
TAB:89:30/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب القول الذي ذكرناه عن ابن عباس والضحاك ،   أن ذلك إنما يقال لهم

TAB:89:30/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r9.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة
TAB:89:30/r9.claim: A Kufan grammarian reads the address as a command to the believing soul at judgment to return to its prepared reward; since it has arrived, the command can function as a statement that it is pleased and approved.
TAB:89:30/r9.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة يتأوّل ذلك يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ بالإيمان ،   والمصدّقة بالثواب والبعث ارجعي

TAB-FULL:v24p395/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r5.claim: Some say an angel speaks these words to the servant as the soul leaves, announcing God's pleasure and the honor prepared for it.
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r5.anchor: وقيل: إن ذلك قول الملك للعبد عند خروج نفسه مبشره برضا ربه عنه

TAB-FULL:v24p395/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r6.claim: After Abū Bakr calls the verse beautiful, the Prophet says an angel will say it to him at death.
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r6.anchor: فقال أبو بكر: إن هذا لحسن، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أما إن الملك سيقولها لك عند الموت»

TAB-FULL:v24p395/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r7.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r7.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ places the return at death and entry among God's servants at the Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v24p395/r7.anchor: عن أبي صالح، {ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية} [الفجر: 28] قال: هذا عند الموت {فادخلي في عبادي} [الفجر: 29] قال هذا يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the reassured spirits return to their bodies on the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية} [الفجر: 28] قال: ترد الأرواح المطمئنة يوم القيامة في الأجساد

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God commands the spirits at Resurrection to return to their bodies and come to Him as first created.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {فادخلي في عبادي وادخلي جنتي} [الفجر: 30] : يأمر الله الأرواح يوم القيامة أن ترجع إلى الأجساد

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r3.claim: ʿIkrima glosses the return as going back to the body.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، في هذه الآية: {ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية} [الفجر: 28] : إلى الجسد

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r4.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ instead places the address at death, with entry among God's servants occurring at Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r4.anchor: عن أبي صالح، {ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية} [الفجر: 28] قال: هذا عند الموت {فادخلي في عبادي} [الفجر: 29] قال: هذا يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the Resurrection interpretation reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk because the next phrase speaks of entering among God's servants and His Garden.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب القول الذي ذكرناه عن ابن عباس والضحاك، أن ذلك إنما يقال لهم عند رد الأرواح في الأجساد يوم البعث

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r9.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r9.claim: Some Kufan grammarians read the reassured soul as faith and affirmation of reward and resurrection, then begin to explain the return as an address to it.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r9.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة يتأول ذلك {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} [الفجر: 27] بالإيمان، والمصدقة بالثواب والبعث ارجعي

TAB-FULL:v24p399/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r1.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r1.claim: The Kufan reading explains the return as going to the reward God prepared; the command can report the soul's already accomplished arrival at the Resurrection, as in saying 'be a Tamīmī' to someone already from that tribe.
TAB-FULL:v24p399/r1.anchor: أعطوا كتبهم بأيمانهم {ارجعي إلى ربك} [الفجر: 28] إلى ما أعد الله لك من الثواب

ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r4.claim: Marḍiyyah derives from the older form marḍwah; the soul is pleased with what God gives, approved, and purified.
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r4.anchor: أصل (مرضية) مرضوة أي راضية بما أتاها، قد رضيت وزكيت.

TABRISI:89:29-30/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r9.speaker: أبو صالح
TABRISI:89:29-30/r9.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says the command to return to the Lord is addressed to the soul at death.
TABRISI:89:29-30/r9.anchor: يقال لها عند الموت عن أبي صالح

TABRISI:89:29-30/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r10.speaker: عكرمة، الضحاك
TABRISI:89:29-30/r10.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk place the return at resurrection.

TABRISI:89:29-30/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r11.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:89:29-30/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets the return as going to the Lord's reward and prepared delights.
TABRISI:89:29-30/r11.anchor: ارجعي إلى ثواب ربك وما أعده لك من النعيم عن الحسن

TABRISI:89:29-30/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:89:29-30/r12.claim: Another interpretation, related from Ibn ʿAbbās, directs the spirit to return to its companion and body.
TABRISI:89:29-30/r12.anchor: إن المراد ارجعي إلى صاحبك وجسدك فيكون الخطاب للروح أن ترجع إلى الجسد

TABRISI:89:29-30/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:29-30/r13.claim: The soul is satisfied with God's reward and its own deeds; another view says it is content with God's decree and pleasing to Him through its actions and beliefs.
TABRISI:89:29-30/r13.anchor: بثواب الله { مرضية } أعمالها التي عملتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r1.speaker: أبو صالح، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r1.claim: At death the soul is told to return to God, pleased with its reward and approved by God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r1.anchor: من الدنيا # يقال لها: ارجعي إلى الله راضية بالثواب (¬1)، مرضية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r2.claim: A report says a man recited the verses before the Prophet, Abu Bakr admired them, and the Prophet told Abu Bakr that an angel would say them to him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r2.anchor: فقال النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: أما إن الملك سيقولها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r4.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r4.claim: Being told to return content and approved occurs at death when the soul is taken.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p527/r4.anchor: قوله: {ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية} تكون عند الوفاة، وقبض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r4.speaker: الحسن، الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r4.claim: Returning to God means returning to His reward and generosity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p529/r4.anchor: وقوله: {ارجعي إلى ربك} أي إلى ثواب ربك وكرامته

WAHIDI-QT:89:28/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:89:28/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:89:28/r1.claim: At death the soul is told to return to its Lord, content with what God gave it.
WAHIDI-QT:89:28/r1.anchor: { ارجعي إلى ربك } يقال لها ذلك عند الموت { راضية } بما آتاها الله

WAHIDI-QT:89:28/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:89:28/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:89:28/r2.claim: The soul is pleasing to its Lord as it leaves this world.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r2.claim: The command to return is addressed to the soul at death; she is content with God's gift and approved by her Lord.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r2.anchor: يقال لها ذلك عند الموت. { راضية } بما آتاها الله { مرضية } رضي عنها ربها.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r3.claim: This address takes place as the soul leaves the world; the next invitation occurs on Judgment Day.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r3.anchor: هذا عند خروجها من الدنيا، فإذا كان يوم القيامة قيل:

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r1.claim: The address is narrated as a future divine saying, preparing the listener for that day; the believer had already found tranquility through faith, sincerity, and offering good to God.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r1.anchor: Bu üslûb-i ifade Kur’ân’ın i‘câzı tarzlarından birisidir. Bunda sâmi‘i derhâl istikbâle hazırlayacak bir telkin vardır

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r2.claim: The tranquil soul returns content with its Lord and accepted by Him, echoing the reciprocal satisfaction of God and the believers.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r2.anchor: sen Rabbinden hoşnut, Rabbin de senden hoşnut

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r10.claim: Some commentators take nafs here to mean the self or essence, while others take it to mean the spirit; mutmainna can accordingly describe either.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r10.anchor: Burada çokları zât mânasına bazıları da rûh mânasına telakkī etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r4.claim: The tranquil soul chooses knowledge of God for God alone and is attached to Him in love, desire, abiding, and speech.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r4.anchor: her kim ma‘rifetullâhı onun gayri bir şey için olmayarak ihtiyar ederse işte o nefs-i mutmainnedir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r5.claim: A tranquil soul is defined by rising through unstable causes to know the First Source, relying only on God, and obeying Him with exclusive sincerity.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r5.anchor: esbâb ve müsebbebât silsilelerinden geçip bizzat müessir olan Mebde’-i A‘lâ’yı mârifete yükselerek

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r6.claim: This definition entails submission to God with excellence, certainty of release from fear and sorrow, and dedicating the self to seek only God’s pleasure.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r6.anchor: Allah için İslâm ve ihsan ile havf u hüzünden

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r7.claim: True freedom means escaping the animal ego, self-reproach, and bondage to anything besides God, then doing every good one can with life and wealth in God’s path.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r7.anchor: nefs-i emmâre tekāzâsından, nefs-i levvâme melâmetinden, mâsivâya esaret kaydlarından kurtarıp

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r10.speaker: Mücâhid
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r10.claim: Mujahid says it is certain that God is its Lord and submits to His command in every deed.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r10.anchor: Mücâhid’den: Allah, rabbi olduğunu musaddık mûkın ve her yaptığı işte O’nun emrine müslim

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r11.claim: Another formulation says the soul is certain God is its Lord, gives its heart only to Him, and has a heart that beats by His command; it is repentant and humble.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r11.anchor: Allah rabbi olduğuna îkān etmiş, gönlünü ancak O’na vermiş, kalbi O’nun emriyle çarpar

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r15.claim: The preceding account contrasts the ignorant, worldly commanding soul and belatedly self-reproaching soul with the tranquil soul that understood truth in time.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r15.anchor: nefs-i emmâre ve nefs-i levvâme hükümleri gösterilmiş, sonra da vaktiyle hakkı anlayıp

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.claim: Exegetes differ on whether this address comes at death, resurrection, or after the reckoning; the author considers the last timing most apparent from the context.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.anchor: Bunda üç kavil vardır: Ölüm zamanında olması, ba‘s zamanında

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r17.claim: On the preferred timing, returning means leaving the place of reckoning for the place God graciously commands, or turning the heart from concern over acceptance to God Himself.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r17.anchor: hesab görülen mevkıften Allah teâlâ’nın inayet ve ikramıyla emir buyurduğu mahalle demektir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r18.claim: The pleased soul is content with the Lord who brought it to eternal bliss; the accepted soul is approved by God for its sound heart and good striving and reaches divine pleasure.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r18.anchor: marziyye de Rabbin indinde marzî ve makbul; yani selîm kalbin, güzel sa‘y ü amelin

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r1.speaker: İkrime
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r1.claim: Ikrima and Dahhak report that the address and command to return occur at resurrection; on this reading the soul returns to its Lord for eternal life.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r1.anchor: İkrime ve Dahhâk’ten rivayet olunduğuna göre bu hitab ile ٱرْجِعِىٓ emri ba‘s sırasındadır

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r4.speaker: İbn Zeyd
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd and many others hold that the address is spoken at the time of death.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r4.anchor: İbn Zeyd ve daha birçokları da bu hitâbın mevt sırasında söyleneceğine kāil olmuşlardır

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r5.speaker: İbn Cübeyr
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r5.claim: Ibn Jubayr reports that when this verse was recited before Abu Bakr, the Prophet told him an angel would say it to him at death.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r5.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem de أَمَا إِنَّ الْمَلَكَ سَيـَقُولُ لَكَ عِنْدَ الْمَوْتِ

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r6.speaker: Hakîm-i Tirmizî
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r6.claim: Hakim al-Tirmidhi transmits a similar report from Abu Bakr through Sulaym ibn Amir.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r6.anchor: b. Aclân tarîkiyle Selim b. Âmir’den, Hazret-i Sıddîk radıyallâhu anh’tan rivayet eylemiştir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r7.claim: If the address occurs at death, nafs means spirit and returning is the spirit’s departure from the body toward its Lord.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r7.anchor: Bu surette “nefs” rûh mânasına olup rücû‘u rûhun bedenden iftirâkıyla Rabbine doğru

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.speaker: Ebû Sâlih
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.claim: Abu Salih says returning to the Lord is at death as departure from the world, while entering among the servants and entering Paradise are commands at resurrection.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.anchor: Bu âyette ٱرْجِعِىٓ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ inde’l-mevttir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.claim: Though Abu Salih’s reading seems apparent, the context favors the address after resurrection and completed reckoning; the reports can fit by treating each death as a person’s resurrection or the commands together as a unit.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.anchor: bu hitâbın da o güne ait olması iktizâ edeceğinden ba‘de’l-ba‘s

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.speaker: Zeyd b. Eslem
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that the tranquil soul is given this address at death, resurrection, and the gathering, and is promised Paradise.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.anchor: mutmainne ölüm sırasında ve ba‘s sırasında ve cem‘günü cennet ile tebşir olunmuştur

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.claim: The majority understand an omitted “God will say” from the preceding context, making the address and commands declarative and creative rather than legislative.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.anchor: cumhûrun muhtârı budur. Buna göre bu hitâbın ve emirlerin teşrî‘î değil tekvînî olması

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.claim: The author also considers a direct, legislative divine address at the surah’s conclusion plausible; separation from what precedes highlights that the tranquil souls themselves should hear it.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.anchor: bunun nüfûs-i mutmainne tarafından re’sen ve bilhassa istimâ‘ı maksud olduğuna tenbih için

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r14.claim: Some exegetes take the address as applying to the tranquil soul in worldly life at all times; the author finds this clearer and more useful.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r14.anchor: bir kısım müfessirîn de bunun nefs-i mutmainneye dünyada da her zaman için hitab olduğuna kāil olmuştur

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r15.claim: On the worldly reading, returning is a voluntary return to God and His decree in every matter, accompanied by contentment in prosperity and adversity.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r15.anchor: rücû‘ile emir rücû‘-i irâdî olarak her işte ve bütün umûrunda râzıye olmak kaydıyla Allah teâlâ’ya

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r16.claim: Explicit contentment is difficult even for the tranquil soul and is the perfection of the content soul; divine acceptance depends on that contentment.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r16.anchor: bu mertebe nefs-i mutmainnenin kemâli mertebesi olan nefs-i râzıye hasleti olduğu

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.claim: The life of a tranquil soul among the righteous is like the ten nights before Eid al-Adha, and its entry into Paradise is the dawn of the greatest festival of bliss.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.anchor: dünya ömrü îd-i adhâya tekaddüm eden bir leyâl-i aşr

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.claim: The commentator prays that he and his readers return to God content and accepted, join His sincere servants, and reach Paradise and the vision of God.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.anchor: bu abd-i hakīri ve bunları hüsn-i nazarla okuyup ona hayırhah olanları

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:28:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:28:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:28:anmerkung/r1.claim: For the root r-ḍ-y, the note refers to 101:7.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:28:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zur Wurzel r-ḍ-y s. die Anmerkung zu 101:7.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.claim: Later verses 27–30 add a positive afterlife ending to the earlier threat-only conclusion, pairing entry into the Garden with the Hell mentioned in verse 23.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.claim: All three insertions use direct speech: the human responds to worldly allotment and threatened Hell, then God's address to the trusting soul and servants supersedes those negative statements.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.anchor: Auffällig ist, dass alle drei Einschübe – V. 15.16, V. 23.24 und V. 27–30 – wörtliche Reden enthalten

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r3.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r3.claim: Neuwirth sees the trusting soul as recalling the oath's worship times, which especially embody confidence and inner calm in God's nearness.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r3.anchor: Neuwirth erblickt in V. 27–30 einen motivischen Rückbezug auf die Schwureinleitung

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.claim: Addressing the person directly without an introductory afterlife formula is a graceful, warm honor that lets the promise of otherworldly happiness reach into this life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.anchor: doğrudan insana hitap edilmesi, Cenâb-ı Hakk’ın bu yapıdaki kullarına çok güzel bir iltifatı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r5.claim: The greatest happiness is perfect servitude that pleases the Lord, followed by God's reward and the believer's own contentment with Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r5.anchor: kulluktaki kemali sayesinde rabbini kendisinden hoşnut etmiş, rabbi tarafından ödüllendirilerek kendisi de O’ndan hoşnut kalmış olmasıdır

ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r1.claim: “Return to your Lord” can mean returning after judgment to the station of divine care and honor, where the blessed wait before each is called to account.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r1.anchor: إرجعي أي من حيث حوسبت إلى ربك أي إلى محل عنايته تعالى وموقف كرامته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, it tells the soul to turn its heart away from anxious concern about its deeds and attend wholly to God; after its accepted reckoning, the words reassure it that the matter is finished.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى ارجعي بتخلية القلب عن الأعمال والألتفات إليها والأهتمام بأمرها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r3.claim: Calling her “the tranquil soul” is a rhetorical prompt, like telling a famous brave person to act bravely when he hesitates; “to your Lord” adds tenderness.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r3.anchor: ونداؤها بعنوان الأطمئنان لتذكيرها بما يقتضي الرجوع نظير قولك لشجاع مشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r4.claim: “Pleased” may mean pleased with God's endless gifts, or specifically relieved by an easy accounting and accepted deeds; al-Alusi says the latter is weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r4.anchor: راضية أي بما يؤتينه من النعم التي لا تتناهى وقد يقال راضية بما نلتيه من خفة الحساب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r5.claim: A view takes the two states as pleased with God and accepted by Him, but al-Alusi questions its fit with the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r5.anchor: وفل قيل المراد راضية عن ربك مرضية عنده وزعم أنه الأظهر واعترض بأنه غير مناسب للسياق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r6.claim: Both adjectives are circumstantial accusatives; the first is apparently prospective, though some take it as simultaneous, and the second advances to the greater divine approval of 9:72.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p130#2/r6.anchor: والوصفان منصوبان على الحال والظاهر أن الحال الأولى مقدرة وقيل مقارنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r5.claim: Some say the address comes at death: the soul is told to return to God, pleased with its reward and pleasing to him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r5.anchor: فقال قوم: يقال لها ذلك عند الموت فيقال لها:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says that as God takes the soul, it becomes at peace with and content toward God, and God is pleased with it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: إذا أراد الله قبضها اطمأنت إلى الله ورضيت عن الله ورضي الله عنها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r7.claim: Ibn Amr reports that a believing soul is greeted at death, leaves fragrant, passes through opened heavenly doors while angels pray for it, prostrates before God, and is placed among believers; its grave is widened and lit, while the unbeliever is sent out foul to wrath and Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r7.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمرو: (1) إذا توفي العبد المؤمن أرسل الله عز وجل ملكين إليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.claim: Abu Salih says ‘return to your Lord’ is spoken when the soul leaves worldly life, while ‘enter among my servants and enter my Paradise’ is spoken at resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو صالح في قوله: "ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية" قال: هذا عند خروجها من الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r9.speaker: عكرمة وعطاء والضحاك وابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r9.claim: Others, including Ikrima, Ata, al-Dahhak, and a report from Ibn Abbas, say the soul is addressed at resurrection and ordered back to its body.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون: إنما يقال لها ذلك عند البعث يقال: ارجعي [إلى ربك] (3)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr recounts Ibn Abbas’s funeral: a strange bird entered the bier and never emerged, and the full ‘tranquil soul’ verses were recited at the grave by an unknown voice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف فشهدت جنازته، فجاء طائر لم [نر] (1)

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r1.claim: Returning to the Lord means returning to His command or to the appointed death/resurrection; the latter wording supports the view that souls existed in a holy realm before bodies.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r1.anchor: إلى أمره أو موعده بالموت، ويشعر ذلك بقول من قال:

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r2.claim: The soul is pleased with what it receives and is approved by God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r2.anchor: بما أوتيت. { مرضية } عند الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.claim: A report promises forgiveness for reciting al-Fajr during the ten nights and a light on the Resurrection Day for reciting it at other times.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.anchor: من قرأ سورة الفجر في الليالي العشر غفر له

BINTSHATI:v2p163/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r9.claim: The believer's soul is content through God's approval; she is both content and approved.
BINTSHATI:v2p163/r9.anchor: ورضى النفس المؤمنة في رضى الله، فهي راضية مرضية.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r6.claim: The soul is content with what it receives and had remained peaceful under both prosperity and hardship, trusting God's decree.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r6.anchor: بما تعطينه . فلا كدر يلحقك بوجه من الوجوه أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r7.claim: It is pleasing to God and creation because it performed righteous deeds while accepting the varied conditions of God's decree.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r7.anchor: عند الله وسائر خلقه , فلا شيء يكرهك بسبب ما كنت مطمئنة

DURR-FULL:v8p513/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the tranquil soul is the believer and interprets its return to its body; when revealed, Abū Bakr praised the verse and the Prophet said it would be said to him.
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} قال: المؤمنة {ارجعي إلى ربك} يقول: إلى جسدك

DURR-FULL:v8p513/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r5.claim: When Abū Bakr praised the verses, the Prophet said an angel would say them to him at death.
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: قرئت عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية}

DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says God invited people to buy the well of Rūma, which ʿUthmān bought and made available for public drinking; the verses were then revealed about him.
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من يشتري بئر رومة نستعذب بها غفر الله له

DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the return to God as souls being restored to bodies on the Day of Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ارجعي إلى ربك} قال: ترد الأرواح يوم القيامة في الأجساد

DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r9.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr describes a stream from the base of the Throne producing earthly creatures; souls then fly and are ordered into bodies, fulfilling the return.
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r9.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال: يسيل واد من أصل العرش فتنبت فيه كل دابة على وجه الأرض

DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the soul is pleased with its reward, God approves its deeds, and it enters among the believers.
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ارجعي إلى ربك راضية} قال: بما أعطيت من الثواب {مرضية} عنها بعملها

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says return to God occurs at death as the soul leaves the world; at resurrection it is told to enter among God’s servants and into Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.anchor: قوله: {ارجعي إلى ربك} قال: هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r6.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the return to God as return to the body.

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r7.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says the believer sees his place in Paradise at death, then is told to return to his body, pleased with the reward until questioned by Munkar and Nakīr.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r7.anchor: بن كعب القرظي في الآية قال: إن المؤمن إذا مات رأى منزله من الجنة

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the believer receives glad tidings of Paradise at death, resurrection, and the gathering.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم رضي الله عنه {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} الآية قال: بشرت بالجنة عند الموت وعند البعث ويوم الجمع

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr recounts a mysterious bird entering Ibn ʿAbbās’s coffin and never being seen again; the tranquil-soul verses were recited at his grave by an unknown person.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال: مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف فجاء طير لم تر عين خلقته فدخل نعشه

TAB:89:28/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:28/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the tranquil souls are returned to their bodies on the Day of Resurrection.
TAB:89:28/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : يا أيّتها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال : تردّ الأرواح المطمئنة يوم القيامة في الأجساد

TAB:89:28/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:89:28/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says God commands souls on the Day of Resurrection to return to their bodies and come to Him as He first created them.
TAB:89:28/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله : فادْخُلِي فِي عبادِي وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي يأمر الله الأرواح يوم القيامة

TAB:89:28/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:89:28/r3.claim: Ikrima interprets the return as a return to the body.
TAB:89:28/r3.anchor: عن عكرِمة في هذه الآية : ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً إلى الجسد

TAB:89:28/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB:89:28/r4.claim: Abu Salih says the soul is addressed at death, while the command to enter among God’s servants is for the Day of Resurrection.
TAB:89:28/r4.anchor: عن أبي صالح ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال : هذا عند الموت فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال : هذا يوم القيامة

TAB:89:28/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r5.speaker: author
TAB:89:28/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the resurrection reading reported from Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak, since the next commands to enter among God’s servants and His garden follow it.
TAB:89:28/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب القول الذي ذكرناه عن ابن عباس والضحاك ، أن ذلك إنما يقال لهم عند ردّ الأرواح

TAB:89:28/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r9.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة
TAB:89:28/r9.claim: Some Kufan grammarians take the soul as secure in faith and belief in resurrection; the command can refer to its prepared reward and function as a report that it is pleased.
TAB:89:28/r9.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة يتأول ذلك يا أيّتها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ بالإيمان ، والمصدقة بالثواب والبعث ارجعي ، تقول لهم الملائكة : إذا أعطوا كتبهم بأيمانهم

TAB:89:28/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r10.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل الكوفة
TAB:89:28/r10.claim: The Kufan explanation compares the imperative to telling a person who is already of one tribe to be Tamimi or Qaysi: the command can be an added connective, as return is effectively a report.
TAB:89:28/r10.anchor: وأنت تقول للرجل : ممن أنت ؟ فيقول : مضريّ ، فتقول : كن تميميا أو قيسيا ، أي أنت من أحد هذين ، فتكون كن صلة ، كذلك الرجوع يكون صلة

ITQAN:v3p97/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p97/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p97/r1.claim: A Qur’anic literal expression is a word kept in its original sense, without inversion or displacement; such wording is common, and its presence is undisputed.
ITQAN:v3p97/r1.anchor: لا خلاف في وقوع الحقائق في القرآن وهي كل لفظ بقي على موضوعه ولا تقديم فيه ولا تأخير وهذا أكثر الكلام

ITQAN:v3p97/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p97/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ITQAN:v3p97/r2.claim: The majority holds that figurative expression occurs in the Qur’an.
ITQAN:v3p97/r2.anchor: وأما المجاز فالجمهور أيضا على وقوعه فيه وأنكره جماعة

ITQAN:v3p97/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p97/r3.speaker: الظاهرية وابن القاص وابن خويز منداد
ITQAN:v3p97/r3.claim: The Zahiris, Ibn al-Qass, and Ibn Khuwayz Mindad deny Qur’anic metaphor, arguing that it resembles falsehood and is used only when literal speech is inadequate, which cannot apply to God.
ITQAN:v3p97/r3.anchor: وأنكره جماعة منهم الظاهرية وابن القاص من الشافعية وابن خويز منداد من المالكية وشبهتهم أن المجاز أخو الكذب

ITQAN:v3p97/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p97/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p97/r4.claim: Suyuti calls this objection false: excluding metaphor would remove half the Qur’an’s beauty; rhetoricians agree it is more eloquent than literal speech, and the objection would also exclude ellipsis, emphasis, and repeated stories.
ITQAN:v3p97/r4.anchor: وهذه شبهة باطلة ولو سقط المجاز من القرآن سقط منه شطر الحسن فقد اتفق البلغاء على أن المجاز أبلغ من الحقيقة

ITQAN:v3p97/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p97/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p97/r5.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam wrote a treatise on metaphor; Suyuti says he summarized it, with extensive additions, in his own book on Qur’anic metaphor.
ITQAN:v3p97/r5.anchor: وقد أفرده بالتصنيف الإمام عز الدين بن عبد السلام ولخصته مع زيادات كثيرة في كتاب سميته ( مجاز الفرسان إلى مجاز القرآن )

ITQAN:v3p97/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p97/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p97/r6.claim: One figurative mode is syntactic or rational attribution: an action is assigned to something associated with its true agent, through their relation.
ITQAN:v3p97/r6.anchor: الأول المجاز في التركيب ويسمى مجاز الإسناد والمجاز العقلي وعلاقته الملابسة وذلك أن يسند الفعل أو شبهه إلى ما هو له أصالة

ITQAN:v3p97/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p97/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p97/r12.claim: Suyuti glosses the Qur’anic phrase “a pleasing life” as “pleased with,” illustrating a passive sense for the adjective rādiyah.

DAMGHANI:v1p297/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p297/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p297/r3.claim: اطمأن can mean to be content; the tranquil soul is content with God's reward.
DAMGHANI:v1p297/r3.anchor: اطمأن بمعنى رضي قوله تعالى في سورة الحج فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به وان أصابته فتنة

NASHR:v2p101/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p101/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p101/r5.claim: In ارجعي and ارجعون, the preceding kasra is incidental, so the rāʾ remains emphatic; the author gives the same rule for ارجعوا and related forms.
NASHR:v2p101/r5.anchor: فهي أيضا في ذلك مفخمة لعروض الكسر قبلها وكون الراء في ذلك أصلها التفخيم

ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r1.claim: “To your Lord” means to the appointment promised by the Lord.
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r1.anchor: { إلى ربك } : أي إلى موعد ربك .

ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r2.claim: Another view takes “Lord” to mean the human being, with the soul returning to enter bodies; nafs is generic.
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r2.anchor: وقيل : الرب هنا الإنسان دون النفس ، أي ادخل في الأجساد ، والنفس اسم جنس .

ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r3.claim: Another view addresses believers now, telling them to persist and strive until they return pleased and accepted by God.
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r3.anchor: وقيل : هذا النداء هو الآن للمؤمنين . لما ذكر حال الكفار قال : يا مؤمنون دوموا وجدوا حتى ترجعوا راضين مرضيين

ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r4.claim: The soul is pleased with what it has received and is pleasing to God.
ABUHAYYAN:89:28/r4.anchor: { راضية } بما أوتيته ، { مرضية } عند الله .

ALUSI:89:28/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:28/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:28/r1.claim: Return means from the place where the soul has been judged.
ALUSI:89:28/r1.anchor: { ارجعى } أي من حيث حوسبت { إلى رَبّكَ }

ALUSI:89:28/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:28/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:28/r2.claim: Your Lord means the place of God's special care and station of honor; reports indicate that the blessed have a special place before accounting where they are spared others' exhaustion and later called to judgment.
ALUSI:89:28/r2.anchor: إلى محل عنايته تعالى وموقف كرامته عز وجل لك أولا وهذا لأن للسعداء قبل الحساب كما يفهم من الأخبار

ALUSI:89:28/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:28/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:28/r3.claim: Alternatively, return means turn solely to God, laying aside concern for one's deeds and whether they will be accepted; the call reassures the soul after its account and acceptance are complete.
ALUSI:89:28/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى ارجعي بتخلية القلب عن الأعمال والالتفات إليها والاهتمام بأمرها أتقبل أم لا

ALUSI:89:28/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:28/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:28/r4.claim: Calling her tranquil reminds her of the quality that should prompt return, like urging a famous brave man to advance; this rationale fits inward return better than return after judgment.
