ALUSI:89:28/r4.anchor: ونداؤها بعنوان الاطمئنان لتذكيرها بما يقتضي الرجوع نظير قولك لشجاع مشهور بالشجاعة

ALUSI:89:28/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:28/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:28/r5.claim: Addressing her as returning to your Lord is especially tender in either interpretation, unlike simply saying return to God.
ALUSI:89:28/r5.anchor: ولا يخفى ما في قوله سبحانه إلى ربك على الوجهين من مزيد اللطف بها

ALUSI:89:28/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:28/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:28/r6.claim: Rāḍiya means content with the endless gifts bestowed on her; contentment with a light account and accepted deeds is also proposed, but al-Ālūsī finds that less persuasive.
ALUSI:89:28/r6.anchor: أي بما تؤتينه من النعم التي لا تتناهى

ALUSI:89:28/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:28/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:89:28/r7.claim: Another view glosses rāḍiya as pleased with her Lord and marḍiyya as pleasing to Him; it is called clearest, though the contextual objection is itself questioned.
ALUSI:89:28/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد راضية عن ربك مرضية عنده وزعم أنه الأظهر واعترض بأنه غير مناسب للسياق

ALUSI:89:28/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:28/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:28/r8.claim: Marḍiyya means approved and well-pleasing to God.

ALUSI:89:28/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:28/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:28/r9.claim: Both adjectives are accusative circumstantial expressions; the first is apparently prospective, though a simultaneous state is also proposed, and the second advances to the greater honor of divine approval, as in 9:72.
ALUSI:89:28/r9.anchor: والوصفان منصوبان على الحال والظاهر أن الحال الأولى مقدرة وقيل مقارنة

ALUSI:89:29/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r5.claim: One reading takes ‘return to your Lord’s promise’ as the promised Garden and company of the righteous, spoken after the reckoning; the objection that this implies prior residence is answered by a potential existence in Adam’s loins while he was in the Garden.
ALUSI:89:29/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى موعد ربك واستظهر أن المراد بموعده تعالى

ALUSI:89:29/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r6.claim: The proposed prior existence is compared with reports from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās that maʿād in 28:85 means Paradise rather than Mecca; this works only if Adam’s Garden was the eschatological Garden, a strongly disputed identification discussed by Ibn al-Qayyim.
ALUSI:89:29/r6.anchor: على ما روى عن أمير المؤمنين علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما من أن المراد بالمعاد الجنة دون مكة

ALUSI:89:29/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r7.claim: Another interpretation makes ‘return to your Lord’s command’ mean return to one of His affairs: His treatment of her without distress, placement in an honored station, or something similar.
ALUSI:89:29/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى أمر ربك واستظهر أن المراد بالأمر على ذلك التقدير

ALUSI:89:29/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r8.claim: A further view understands the return as return to God’s general favor, from the barzakh after death or from the period after resurrection but before judgment.
ALUSI:89:29/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى كرامة ربك ويراد جنس كرامته سبحانه

ALUSI:89:29/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r9.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
ALUSI:89:29/r9.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk place the address at resurrection; on one analysis nafs means the person, Lord means God, and an implied noun supplies the station to which she returns.
ALUSI:89:29/r9.anchor: وعن عكرمة والضحاك أن ذلك القول عند البعث فقيل النفس بمعنى الذات أيضاً والمراد بالرب هو الله عز وجل

ALUSI:89:29/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r10.claim: Another analysis takes nafs as the soul and rabb as its owner, the body: the soul returns to its former body, then enters the servants and the abode of reward.
ALUSI:89:29/r10.anchor: وقيل النفس بمعنى الروح والمراد بالرب الصاحب وفسر بالجسد وباقي الآية على حاله

ALUSI:89:29/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r12.speaker: ابن زيد وجماعة
ALUSI:89:29/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd and a group say the address comes at death, with the soul understood as the spirit returning to the sacred realm and then joining the close servants.
ALUSI:89:29/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وجماعة إن ذلك القول عند الموت

ALUSI:89:29/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:89:29/r13.claim: Ibn Jubayr reports that, after the tranquil-soul verse was recited before him, Abū Bakr called it beautiful and the Prophet said an angel would address him with it at death; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:89:29/r13.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أما أن الملك سيقولها لك عند الموت

ALUSI:89:29/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r14.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
ALUSI:89:29/r14.claim: A similar death-time report is transmitted in al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī’s Nawādir al-uṣūl through Thābit ibn ʿAjlān and Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir from Abū Bakr; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:89:29/r14.anchor: من طريق ثابت بن عجلان عن سليم بن عامر عن الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI:89:29/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r18.speaker: أبو صالح
ALUSI:89:29/r18.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says the return is at death, meaning departure from worldly life, while the two entry commands are spoken at resurrection.
ALUSI:89:29/r18.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن أبي صالح أنه قال في الآية

ALUSI:89:29/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r19.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
ALUSI:89:29/r19.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī places the address after death but before resurrection: the believer sees his Garden home, returns to the body, and awaits questioning by Munkar and Nakīr; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:89:29/r19.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن محمد بن كعب القرظي أنه قال في الآية إن المؤمن إذا مات

ALUSI:89:29/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r21.claim: An inward reading applies the commands throughout earthly life: turn to God in every matter, join the sincere servants through good works, and enter the Garden potentially; al-Ālūsī says this is not a sound interpretation.
ALUSI:89:29/r21.anchor: وقيل يجوز أن يكون ذلك في سائر أوقات النفس في حياتها الدنيا

ALUSI:89:29/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r25.claim: Some readings imply that souls existed before bodies in the realm of dominion; al-Ālūsī notes that most theologians, like Plato and his followers, instead hold that souls are created when bodies become ready for them.
ALUSI:89:29/r25.anchor: وجمهور المتكلمين على أنها مخلوقة عند استعداد الأبدان لها وكذا أفلاطون وأصحابه

ALUSI:89:30/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r5.claim: One reading takes ‘return to your Lord’s promise’ as the promised Garden and company of the righteous, spoken after the reckoning; the objection that this implies prior residence is answered by a potential existence in Adam’s loins while he was in the Garden.
ALUSI:89:30/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى موعد ربك واستظهر أن المراد بموعده تعالى

ALUSI:89:30/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r6.claim: The proposed prior existence is compared with reports from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās that maʿād in 28:85 means Paradise rather than Mecca; this works only if Adam’s Garden was the eschatological Garden, a strongly disputed identification discussed by Ibn al-Qayyim.
ALUSI:89:30/r6.anchor: على ما روى عن أمير المؤمنين علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما من أن المراد بالمعاد الجنة دون مكة

ALUSI:89:30/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r7.claim: Another interpretation makes ‘return to your Lord’s command’ mean return to one of His affairs: His treatment of her without distress, placement in an honored station, or something similar.
ALUSI:89:30/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى أمر ربك واستظهر أن المراد بالأمر على ذلك التقدير

ALUSI:89:30/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r8.claim: A further view understands the return as return to God’s general favor, from the barzakh after death or from the period after resurrection but before judgment.
ALUSI:89:30/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى كرامة ربك ويراد جنس كرامته سبحانه

ALUSI:89:30/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r9.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
ALUSI:89:30/r9.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk place the address at resurrection; on one analysis nafs means the person, Lord means God, and an implied noun supplies the station to which she returns.
ALUSI:89:30/r9.anchor: وعن عكرمة والضحاك أن ذلك القول عند البعث فقيل النفس بمعنى الذات أيضاً والمراد بالرب هو الله عز وجل

ALUSI:89:30/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r10.claim: Another analysis takes nafs as the soul and rabb as its owner, the body: the soul returns to its former body, then enters the servants and the abode of reward.
ALUSI:89:30/r10.anchor: وقيل النفس بمعنى الروح والمراد بالرب الصاحب وفسر بالجسد وباقي الآية على حاله

ALUSI:89:30/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r12.speaker: ابن زيد وجماعة
ALUSI:89:30/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd and a group say the address comes at death, with the soul understood as the spirit returning to the sacred realm and then joining the close servants.
ALUSI:89:30/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وجماعة إن ذلك القول عند الموت

ALUSI:89:30/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:89:30/r13.claim: Ibn Jubayr reports that, after the tranquil-soul verse was recited before him, Abū Bakr called it beautiful and the Prophet said an angel would address him with it at death; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:89:30/r13.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أما أن الملك سيقولها لك عند الموت

ALUSI:89:30/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r14.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
ALUSI:89:30/r14.claim: A similar death-time report is transmitted in al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī’s Nawādir al-uṣūl through Thābit ibn ʿAjlān and Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir from Abū Bakr; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:89:30/r14.anchor: من طريق ثابت بن عجلان عن سليم بن عامر عن الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI:89:30/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r18.speaker: أبو صالح
ALUSI:89:30/r18.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says the return is at death, meaning departure from worldly life, while the two entry commands are spoken at resurrection.
ALUSI:89:30/r18.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن أبي صالح أنه قال في الآية

ALUSI:89:30/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r19.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
ALUSI:89:30/r19.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī places the address after death but before resurrection: the believer sees his Garden home, returns to the body, and awaits questioning by Munkar and Nakīr; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:89:30/r19.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن محمد بن كعب القرظي أنه قال في الآية إن المؤمن إذا مات

ALUSI:89:30/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r21.claim: An inward reading applies the commands throughout earthly life: turn to God in every matter, join the sincere servants through good works, and enter the Garden potentially; al-Ālūsī says this is not a sound interpretation.
ALUSI:89:30/r21.anchor: وقيل يجوز أن يكون ذلك في سائر أوقات النفس في حياتها الدنيا

ALUSI:89:30/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r25.claim: Some readings imply that souls existed before bodies in the realm of dominion; al-Ālūsī notes that most theologians, like Plato and his followers, instead hold that souls are created when bodies become ready for them.
ALUSI:89:30/r25.anchor: وجمهور المتكلمين على أنها مخلوقة عند استعداد الأبدان لها وكذا أفلاطون وأصحابه

BAGHAWI:89:27/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:27/r7.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI:89:27/r7.claim: One group says the address is spoken at death: return to God, content with the reward and pleasing to Him.
BAGHAWI:89:27/r7.anchor: فقال قوم : يقال لها ذلك عند الموت فيقال لها : { ارجعي إلى ربك } إلى الله

BAGHAWI:89:27/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:27/r8.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI:89:27/r8.claim: Al-Hasan describes the soul at God's taking it as tranquil toward God, content with Him, and itself pleasing to Him.
BAGHAWI:89:27/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن : إذا أراد الله قبضها اطمأنت إلى الله ورضيت عن الله ورضي الله عنها .

BAGHAWI:89:27/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:27/r9.speaker: عبد الله ابن عمر
BAGHAWI:89:27/r9.claim: Ibn Umar describes the believer's soul welcomed at death by angels, brought to God, and placed with believers in a fragrant, spacious grave; the disbeliever's soul is sent out amid stench and threatened with Hell and God's anger.
BAGHAWI:89:27/r9.anchor: قال عبد الله ابن عمر : إذا توفي العبد المؤمن أرسل الله عز وجل ملكين ،   وأرسل إليه بتحفة من الجنة

BAGHAWI:89:27/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:27/r10.speaker: أبو صالح
BAGHAWI:89:27/r10.claim: Abu Salih says the return address is spoken as the soul leaves this world, while entry among God's servants and into His garden is said at the Resurrection.
BAGHAWI:89:27/r10.anchor: وقال أبو صالح في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية } قال : هذا عند خروجها من الدنيا

BAGHAWI:89:27/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:27/r11.speaker: آخرون
BAGHAWI:89:27/r11.claim: Another group places the address at resurrection, when souls are ordered to return to their bodies; this is attributed to Ikrima, Ata, al-Dahhak, and al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas.
BAGHAWI:89:27/r11.anchor: وقال آخرون : إنما يقال لها ذلك عند البعث .   { ارجعي إلى ربك } أي إلى صاحبك وجسدك

BAGHAWI:89:27/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:27/r12.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI:89:27/r12.claim: Al-Hasan also interprets return as return to God's reward: the soul is content with what God prepared, and God is pleased with it.
BAGHAWI:89:27/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن : معناه : ارجعي إلى ثواب ربك راضيةً عن الله بما أعد لها ،   مرضيةً رضي الله عنها ربها .

BAGHAWI:89:28/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:28/r7.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI:89:28/r7.claim: One group says the address is spoken at death: return to God, content with the reward and pleasing to Him.
BAGHAWI:89:28/r7.anchor: فقال قوم : يقال لها ذلك عند الموت فيقال لها : { ارجعي إلى ربك } إلى الله

BAGHAWI:89:28/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:28/r8.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI:89:28/r8.claim: Al-Hasan describes the soul at God's taking it as tranquil toward God, content with Him, and itself pleasing to Him.
BAGHAWI:89:28/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن : إذا أراد الله قبضها اطمأنت إلى الله ورضيت عن الله ورضي الله عنها .

BAGHAWI:89:28/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:28/r9.speaker: عبد الله ابن عمر
BAGHAWI:89:28/r9.claim: Ibn Umar describes the believer's soul welcomed at death by angels, brought to God, and placed with believers in a fragrant, spacious grave; the disbeliever's soul is sent out amid stench and threatened with Hell and God's anger.
BAGHAWI:89:28/r9.anchor: قال عبد الله ابن عمر : إذا توفي العبد المؤمن أرسل الله عز وجل ملكين ،   وأرسل إليه بتحفة من الجنة

BAGHAWI:89:28/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:28/r10.speaker: أبو صالح
BAGHAWI:89:28/r10.claim: Abu Salih says the return address is spoken as the soul leaves this world, while entry among God's servants and into His garden is said at the Resurrection.
BAGHAWI:89:28/r10.anchor: وقال أبو صالح في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية } قال : هذا عند خروجها من الدنيا

BAGHAWI:89:28/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:28/r11.speaker: آخرون
BAGHAWI:89:28/r11.claim: Another group places the address at resurrection, when souls are ordered to return to their bodies; this is attributed to Ikrima, Ata, al-Dahhak, and al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas.
BAGHAWI:89:28/r11.anchor: وقال آخرون : إنما يقال لها ذلك عند البعث .   { ارجعي إلى ربك } أي إلى صاحبك وجسدك

BAGHAWI:89:28/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:28/r12.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI:89:28/r12.claim: Al-Hasan also interprets return as return to God's reward: the soul is content with what God prepared, and God is pleased with it.
BAGHAWI:89:28/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن : معناه : ارجعي إلى ثواب ربك راضيةً عن الله بما أعد لها ،   مرضيةً رضي الله عنها ربها .

BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that at Ibn Abbas's funeral in Taif a strange bird entered his bier and was not seen leaving; these verses were recited at his grave, though the reciter was unknown.
BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : مات ابن عباس بالطائف فشهدت جنازته ،   فجاء طائر لم ير على صورة خلقه فدخل نعشه

BAYDAWI:89:28/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:28/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:28/r1.claim: Return may mean to God's command or appointed time, identified with death, or the resurrection.
BAYDAWI:89:28/r1.anchor: إلى أمره أو موعده بالموت ويشعر ذلك بقول من قال كانت النفوس قبل الأبدان موجودة

BAYDAWI:89:28/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:28/r2.speaker: من قال
BAYDAWI:89:28/r2.claim: The wording suggests the view that souls existed in the holy realm before bodies.
BAYDAWI:89:28/r2.anchor: بقول من قال كانت النفوس قبل الأبدان موجودة في عالم القدس

BAYDAWI:89:28/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:28/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:28/r3.claim: The soul is content with what it has been given and is approved by God.
BAYDAWI:89:28/r3.anchor: راضية بما أوتيت مرضية عند الله تعالى

BIQAI:89:28/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:28/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:28/r1.claim: “Return to your Lord” may mean resurrection to the appointed meeting with the Creator who brought the soul into being and nurtured it among the successful.
BIQAI:89:28/r1.anchor: موعد الذي أوجدك ورباك تربية الموفقين

BIQAI:89:28/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:28/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:28/r2.claim: Alternatively, the return may be to the body from which the soul departed.

BIQAI:89:28/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:28/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:28/r3.claim: The soul is content with what it receives and accepted by God and creation for its righteous conduct; as in worldly life, it remained calm and satisfied under God's decree, sweet or bitter.
BIQAI:89:28/r3.anchor: كما كنت في دار القلق والاضطراب مطمئنة ساكنة تحت القضاء والقدر

DURR:89:27/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:27/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:27/r1.claim: In a report through Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas says the reassured soul is the believer and the return is to its body; Abu Bakr admires the verse, and the Prophet says it will be said to him.
DURR:89:27/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } قال : المؤمنة { ارجعي إلى ربك } يقول : إلى جسدك

DURR:89:27/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:27/r2.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:27/r2.claim: After Abu Bakr praises the verse, the Prophet tells him an angel will say it to him at death.
DURR:89:27/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «أما إن الملك سيقولها لك عند الموت »

DURR:89:27/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:27/r3.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:27/r3.claim: Abu Bakr recounts reading the verse to the Prophet, who tells him the angel will say it to him when he dies.
DURR:89:27/r3.anchor: فقلت : ما أحسن هذا يا رسول الله ، فقال : «يا أبا بكر أما إن الملك سيقولها لك عند الموت

DURR:89:27/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:27/r10.speaker: أبيّ
DURR:89:27/r10.claim: Ubayy's reading adds 'secure' before 'reassured' and reads 'enter among My servant' in the singular.
DURR:89:27/r10.anchor: عن أبي الشيخ الهنائي رضي الله عنه

DURR:89:27/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:27/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:27/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the following command with 'My servant' in the singular.
DURR:89:27/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قرأها «فادخلي في عبدي على التوحيد

DURR:89:28/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:28/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the return to God as souls being returned to their bodies on the Day of Resurrection.
DURR:89:28/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : ترد الأرواح يوم القيامة في الأجساد

DURR:89:28/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:89:28/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr describes a river flowing from beneath the Throne, from which creatures grow; spirits then fly and are commanded to enter their bodies, explaining this return.
DURR:89:28/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال : يسيل واد من أصل العرش

DURR:89:28/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:28/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the soul is pleased with the reward given, approved because of its deeds, and told to enter among the believing servants.
DURR:89:28/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك راضية }

DURR:89:28/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:28/r4.claim: Hasan says at a believer's death the soul finds rest in God, is pleased with Him and He with it; God takes it, admits it to Paradise, and makes it one of His righteous servants.
DURR:89:28/r4.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } الآية ، قال : إن الله إذا أراد قبض عبده المؤمن اطمأنت النفس إليه

DURR:89:28/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR:89:28/r5.claim: Abu Salih locates the soul's return to God at death as it leaves the world; the commands to join God's servants and enter Paradise come on the Day of Resurrection.
DURR:89:28/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

DURR:89:28/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r6.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:28/r6.claim: The Prophet teaches a supplication asking God for a reassured soul that believes in meeting Him, accepts His decree, and is content with His provision.
DURR:89:28/r6.anchor: عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لرجل : «قل اللهم إني أسألك نفساً مطمئنة

DURR:89:28/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r10.speaker: الضحاك
DURR:89:28/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the return to God as return to the body.
DURR:89:28/r10.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : إلى جسدك

DURR:89:28/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r11.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR:89:28/r11.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says a believer sees their place in Paradise at death, then is told to return to the body, pleased by the reward seen and approved until Munkar and Nakir question them.
DURR:89:28/r11.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي في الآية قال : إن المؤمن إذا مات رأى منزله من الجنة

DURR:89:28/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r13.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR:89:28/r13.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the believer receives glad tidings of Paradise at death, at resurrection, and on the Day of Gathering.
DURR:89:28/r13.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم رضي الله عنه { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } الآية قال : بشرت بالجنة عند الموت وعند البعث ويوم الجمع

DURR:89:28/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:89:28/r14.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr recounts that an unfamiliar bird entered Ibn Abbas's bier and was never seen leaving; as Ibn Abbas was buried, this passage was recited at the grave edge by an unknown speaker.
DURR:89:28/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال : مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف

DURR:89:29/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:29/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the souls return to their bodies on the Day of Resurrection.
DURR:89:29/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : ترد الأرواح يوم القيامة

DURR:89:29/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:89:29/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr describes a valley flowing from beneath the Throne where creatures grow; souls then fly and are ordered into their bodies.
DURR:89:29/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال : يسيل واد من أصل العرش ،   فتنبت فيه كل دابة على وجه الأرض

DURR:89:29/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:29/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the soul is content with the reward it received, approved because of its deeds, and enters among the believers.
DURR:89:29/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك راضية } قال : بما أعطيت من الثواب

DURR:89:29/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR:89:29/r5.claim: Abu Salih distinguishes the soul's return at death, as it leaves worldly life, from the command at Resurrection to enter God's servants and Paradise.
DURR:89:29/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

DURR:89:29/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r10.speaker: الضحاك
DURR:89:29/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the command to return to one's Lord as a command to return to one's body.
DURR:89:29/r10.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : إلى جسدك

DURR:89:29/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r11.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR:89:29/r11.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says a believer sees his place in Paradise at death; God tells the soul to return to its body, satisfied with its reward and approved until Munkar and Nakir question it.
DURR:89:29/r11.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي في الآية قال : إن المؤمن إذا مات رأى منزله من الجنة فيقول تبارك وتعالى

DURR:89:29/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:89:29/r14.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that after Ibn Abbas died at Taif, an extraordinary bird entered his bier and was never seen leaving; after burial someone unknown recited this passage at his grave.
DURR:89:29/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال : مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف ،   فجاء طير لم تر عين خلقته

DURR:89:30/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:30/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:30/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the souls return to their bodies on the Day of Resurrection.
DURR:89:30/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : ترد الأرواح يوم القيامة

DURR:89:30/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:30/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:89:30/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr describes a valley flowing from beneath the Throne where creatures grow; souls then fly and are ordered into their bodies.
DURR:89:30/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال : يسيل واد من أصل العرش ،   فتنبت فيه كل دابة على وجه الأرض

DURR:89:30/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:30/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:30/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the soul is content with the reward it received, approved because of its deeds, and enters among the believers.
DURR:89:30/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك راضية } قال : بما أعطيت من الثواب

DURR:89:30/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:30/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR:89:30/r5.claim: Abu Salih distinguishes the soul's return at death, as it leaves worldly life, from the command at Resurrection to enter God's servants and Paradise.
DURR:89:30/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

DURR:89:30/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:30/r10.speaker: الضحاك
DURR:89:30/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the command to return to one's Lord as a command to return to one's body.
DURR:89:30/r10.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : إلى جسدك

DURR:89:30/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:30/r11.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR:89:30/r11.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says a believer sees his place in Paradise at death; God tells the soul to return to its body, satisfied with its reward and approved until Munkar and Nakir question it.
DURR:89:30/r11.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي في الآية قال : إن المؤمن إذا مات رأى منزله من الجنة فيقول تبارك وتعالى

DURR:89:30/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:30/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:89:30/r14.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that after Ibn Abbas died at Taif, an extraordinary bird entered his bier and was never seen leaving; after burial someone unknown recited this passage at his grave.
DURR:89:30/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال : مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف ،   فجاء طير لم تر عين خلقته

IBNASHUR:89:28/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r1.claim: The address is voiced on the Day of Resurrection from the sacred presence, either by God or by the angels.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r1.anchor: فهذا قول يصدر يوم القيامة من جانب القدس

IBNASHUR:89:28/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r2.claim: If God speaks, naming the Lord instead of using a pronoun underscores intimate care and honors the addressed soul through the possessive relation.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r2.anchor: إظهاراً في مقام الإِضمار بقرينة تفريع

IBNASHUR:89:28/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r3.claim: If angels speak, ‘your Lord’ is the expected wording; the following ‘enter among My servants’ is God's prompting that confirms their words.

IBNASHUR:89:28/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r4.claim: Returning to God figuratively means dwelling in honored Paradise, like a host's home; the soul earned it through promised good deeds and had been away in worldly life, so this is a special return rather than mere afterlife arrival.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r4.anchor: والرجوع إلى الله مستعار للكون في نعيم الجنة التي هي دار الكرامة عند الله

IBNASHUR:89:28/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r5.claim: The image of an honored dwelling is illustrated by the seat of truth with the Mighty King.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r5.anchor: دار الكرامة عند الله بمنزلة دار المضيف قال تعالى

IBNASHUR:89:28/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r6.claim: Alternatively, this may begin a new address to the tranquil souls of believers, prompted by the preceding mention of punishment for the disbelieving human.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الآية استئنافاً ابتدائياً جرى على مناسبة ذكر عذاب الإنسان المشرك

IBNASHUR:89:28/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r7.claim: The command to return is meant as a promise qualified by the following states, ‘pleased’ and ‘approved’; return is figurative on this reading.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r7.anchor: مراد منه تقييده بالحالين بعده وهما

IBNASHUR:89:28/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r9.speaker: الضحاك
IBNASHUR:89:28/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse was revealed about Uthman ibn Affan when he donated the well of Rumah.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r9.anchor: أنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان لما تصدق ببئرِ رومة

IBNASHUR:89:28/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r10.speaker: بريدة
IBNASHUR:89:28/r10.claim: Buraydah says the verse was revealed about Hamza when he was killed.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r10.anchor: أنها نزلت في حمزة حين قُتل

IBNASHUR:89:28/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r11.claim: Another report identifies Khubayb ibn Adi when the people of Mecca crucified him.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r11.anchor: نزلت في خُبَيب بن عدي لما صلبه أهل مكة

IBNASHUR:89:28/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r12.claim: The sūra is agreed to be Meccan, though al-Dani transmits from some scholars that it is Medinan.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r12.anchor: والاتفاق على أن السورة مكية إلا ما رواه الداني عن بعض العلماء أنها مدنية

IBNASHUR:89:28/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r13.claim: If the verse is Medinan, it is either detached from what precedes by a specific divine arrangement or revealed later because of thematic fit.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r13.anchor: وهي على هذا منفصلة عما قبلها كتبت هنا بتوقيف خاص أو نزلت عقب ما قبلها للمناسبة

IBNASHUR:89:28/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن حارثة وأبي بن كعب وابن مسعود
IBNASHUR:89:28/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas, Zayd ibn Harithah, Ubayy ibn Kab, and Ibn Masud say this is said at resurrection as spirits return to bodies.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r14.anchor: أن هذا يقال عند البعث لترجع الأرواح في الأجساد

IBNASHUR:89:28/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r15.claim: On the resurrection reading, the passage continues the account of the earth being crushed; return is literal and ‘Lord’ means the soul's possessor, its body.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r15.anchor: والرجوع على هذا حقيقة والرب مراد به صاحب النفس وهو الجسد

IBNASHUR:89:28/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r16.speaker: زيد بن حارثة وأبو صالح
IBNASHUR:89:28/r16.claim: Zayd ibn Harithah and Abu Salih say the address is spoken to the soul at death.

IBNASHUR:89:28/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r17.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:89:28/r17.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr relates that a man recited the verse, Abu Bakr praised it, and the Prophet said an angel would say it to Abu Bakr at death.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r17.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم « أمَا إنَّ الملَك سيقولها لك عند الموت

IBNASHUR:89:28/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r18.speaker: زيد بن حارثة
IBNASHUR:89:28/r18.claim: Zayd ibn Harithah says the words greet a believer's soul at death with glad tidings of Paradise.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r18.anchor: وعن زيد بن حارثة أن هذا يقال لنفس المؤمن عند الموت تبشر بالجنة

IBNASHUR:89:28/r31.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r31.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r31.claim: The soul is pleased with the honor it receives, implying that it is given everything it desires.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r31.anchor: وهو كناية عن إعطائها كل ما تطمح إليه

IBNASHUR:89:28/r32.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r32.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r32.claim: Mardiyya is a passive participle originally meaning ‘one approved of’; deletion and verbal connection remove the preposition and make it the grammatical subject.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r32.anchor: والمرضية : اسم مفعول وأصله : مَرضياً عنها

IBNASHUR:89:28/r33.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r33.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r33.claim: Being approved adds praise and implies that the one pleased with her increases His gifts beyond what she already finds satisfactory.
IBNASHUR:89:28/r33.anchor: والمقصود من هذا الوصف زيادة الثناء مع الكناية عن الزيادة في إفاضة الإنعام

IBNATIYYA:89:27/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:27/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:27/r1.claim: After describing the punished, God turns to the souls of believers and their condition.
IBNATIYYA:89:27/r1.anchor: ولما فرغ ذكر هؤلاء المعذبين عقب تعالى بذكر نفوس المؤمنين وحالهم

IBNATIYYA:89:28/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r1.claim: On the view that the address comes at death, “return to your Lord” means return through death.
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r1.anchor: ومعنى ( ارجعي إلى ربك ) على هذا التأويل ( ارجعي ) بالموت

IBNATIYYA:89:28/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r3.claim: Another group places the address at the resurrection of bodies and takes the return as rising from death to God.
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r3.anchor: وقال قوم النداء عند قيام الأجساد من القبور فقوله تعالى : ( ارجعي إلى ربك ) معناه : بالبعث من موتك ارجعي إلى الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:89:28/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r4.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r4.claim: Some take rabb as the human body containing the soul: “return to your Lord” means enter the bodies, with nafs used generically; Ibn Abbas's singular reading and Ibn Masud's “in my servant's body” support this.
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r4.anchor: وقيل الرب هنا : الإنسان ذو النفس ، أي : ادخلي في الأجساد ، و ( النفس ) اسم جنس

IBNATIYYA:89:28/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r5.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r5.claim: Another view makes the address a present exhortation to believers, as a counterpart to the description of disbelievers: persist and strive until you return satisfied and approved; nafs is generic here too.
IBNATIYYA:89:28/r5.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء : هذا النداء هو الآن للمؤمنين كما ذكر الله تعالى حال الكافرين قال : يا مؤمنون

IBNATIYYA:89:29/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r6.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r6.claim: Others place the call at the gathering when those bound for Hell are led away; the souls are addressed together with their owners, “return” means to God's mercy, and the servants are the righteous and God-fearing.
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون : هذا النداء إنما هو الموقف عندما ينطلق بأهل النار إلى النار ، فنداء النفوس على هذا إنما هو نداء أرباب النفوس مع النفوس

IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.claim: Others place the address at the gathering when people bound for Hell are led away; the souls are addressed with their owners, return is to God's mercy, and the servants are the righteous and God-fearing.
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون : هذا النداء إنما هو الموقف عندما ينطلق بأهل النار إلى النار ، فنداء النفوس على هذا إنما هو نداء أرباب النفوس مع النفوس

IBNKATHIR:89:27/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r2.claim: Returning to the Lord means returning to His nearness, reward, and what He has prepared for His people in Paradise.
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r2.anchor: أي : إلى جواره وثوابه وما أعد لعباده في جنته

IBNKATHIR:89:27/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r3.claim: Rāḍiya means content within herself; marḍiyya means she is content with God, whom she pleases and who is pleased with her.
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r3.anchor: أي : في نفسها { مَرْضِيَّةً } أي : قد رضيت عن الله ورضي عنها وأرضاها

IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.claim: God calls the soul to join His servants and enter Paradise; this address comes at death and again on Resurrection, as angels announce the believer at death and rising from the grave.
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.anchor: وهذا يقال لها عند الاحتضار ، وفي يوم القيامة أيضا ، كما أن الملائكة يبشرون المؤمن عند احتضاره

IBNKATHIR:89:27/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r7.claim: In al-ʿAwfī’s report, Ibn ʿAbbās explains the address to tranquil souls on Resurrection as a call to return to their companion, the body they inhabited in worldly life.

IBNKATHIR:89:27/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r11.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r11.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr’s mursal report says the Prophet told Abū Bakr that the angel would say these words to him at death; Ibn Kathir calls the report good (ḥasan).
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r11.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : " أما إن الملك سيقول لك هذا عند الموت "

KASHSHAF:89:28/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:28/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:28/r1.claim: Return to your Lord's appointed meeting, content with what you have received and accepted by God.
KASHSHAF:89:28/r1.anchor: على معنى : ارجعي إلى موعد ربك

MAWARDI:89:28/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:28/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:89:28/r1.claim: The soul is told to return to its body at resurrection.
MAWARDI:89:28/r1.anchor: أحدهما : إلى جسدك عند البعث في القيامة ،   قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI:89:28/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:28/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
MAWARDI:89:28/r2.claim: Alternatively, it is told to return to its Lord at death in worldly life.
MAWARDI:89:28/r2.anchor: الثاني : إلى ربك عند الموت في الدنيا ،   قاله أبو صالح

MAWARDI:89:28/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:28/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:89:28/r3.claim: Māwardī also suggests a return to the reward of the Lord in the afterlife.
MAWARDI:89:28/r3.anchor: ويحتمل تأويلاً ثالثاً : إلى ثواب ربك في الآخرة .

MAWARDI:89:28/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:28/r4.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:89:28/r4.claim: The soul is pleased with God, and God is pleased with it.
MAWARDI:89:28/r4.anchor: أحدهما : رضيت عن الله ورضي عنها ،   قاله الحسن

MAWARDI:89:28/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:28/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:89:28/r5.claim: The soul is pleased with God's reward, and God is pleased with its deeds.
MAWARDI:89:28/r5.anchor: الثاني : رضيت بثواب الله ورضي بعملها ،   قاله ابن عباس

NASAFI:89:28/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:28/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:28/r1.claim: “Return to your Lord” can mean return to the appointed meeting with Him.
NASAFI:89:28/r1.anchor: { ارجعى إلى } موعد { رَبِّكِ } أو ثواب ربك

NASAFI:89:28/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:28/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:28/r2.claim: Alternatively, return to your Lord means return to His reward.
NASAFI:89:28/r2.anchor: { ارجعى إلى } موعد { رَبِّكِ } أو ثواب ربك

NASAFI:89:28/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:28/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:28/r3.claim: The soul is pleased with God for what it has been given.

NASAFI:89:28/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:28/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:28/r4.claim: It is pleasing to God because of what it did.

QURTUBI:89:28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:28/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وعطاء
QURTUBI:89:28/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and Ata take the return to be to the soul's companion and body; al-Tabari prefers this view, placing the return at resurrection.
QURTUBI:89:28/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " ارجعي إلى ربك " أي إلى صاحبك وجسدك . قاله ابن عباس وعكرمة وعطاء . واختاره الطبري

QURTUBI:89:28/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:28/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:89:28/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas's singular reading في عبدي in the next verse supports return to the body; God will command souls at resurrection to return to their bodies.
QURTUBI:89:28/r2.anchor: ودليله قراءة ابن عباس " فادخلي في عبدي " على التوحيد ، فيأمر اللّه تعالى الأرواح غدا أن ترجع إلى الأجساد

QURTUBI:89:28/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:28/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI:89:28/r3.claim: Ibn Masud's reading in the next verse says في جسد عبدي, explicitly referring to the servant's body.
QURTUBI:89:28/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود " في جسد عبدي "

QURTUBI:89:28/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:28/r4.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI:89:28/r4.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the return as reaching the Lord's reward and generosity.
QURTUBI:89:28/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن : ارجعي إلى ثواب ربك وكرامته

QURTUBI:89:28/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:28/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
QURTUBI:89:28/r5.claim: Abu Salih says it means returning to God, and places this at death.
QURTUBI:89:28/r5.anchor: وقال أبو صالح : المعنى : ارجعي إلى اللّه . وهذا عند الموت

RAZI:89:27/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:27/r19.speaker: author
RAZI:89:27/r19.claim: If the soul is incorporeal, its coming and return mean taking up and relinquishing governance; if it is a subtle body, the description is literal.
RAZI:89:27/r19.anchor: يكون وصفها بالمجيء والرجوع بمعنى التدبير وتركه

RAZI:89:28/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:28/r1.speaker: من القدماء
RAZI:89:28/r1.claim: Some ancient thinkers argued that souls are eternal, reasoning that “return to your Lord” implies existence before the body.
RAZI:89:28/r1.anchor: من القدماء من زعم أن النفوس أزلية

RAZI:89:28/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:28/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:89:28/r2.claim: If the address occurs at death, it supports the precedence of souls over bodies, but precedence does not prove eternity.

RAZI:89:28/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:28/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:89:28/r3.claim: If the address occurs at resurrection, “return” means return to the Lord’s reward and reenter the body from which the soul departed.

RAZI:89:28/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:28/r4.speaker: المجسمة
RAZI:89:28/r4.claim: Anthropomorphists use the directional phrase and the endpoint sense of إلى to argue that God occupies a spatial direction.

RAZI:89:28/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:28/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:89:28/r5.claim: The phrase can mean return to God’s judgment, reward, or beneficence, rather than movement toward a place.
RAZI:89:28/r5.anchor: إلى حكم ربك ،   أو إلى ثواب ربك أو إلى إحسان ربك

RAZI:89:28/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:28/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:89:28/r6.claim: The intellect ascends through beings and causes until it reaches the Necessary Existent, where goals and motion end.
RAZI:89:28/r6.anchor: القوة العقلية بسيرها العقلي تترقى من موجود إلى موجود آخر

RAZI:89:28/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:28/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:89:28/r7.claim: The soul is content with its reward, and God is pleased with the deeds it performed in worldly life.
RAZI:89:28/r7.anchor: فالمعنى راضية بالثواب مرضية عنك في الأعمال

RAZI:89:28/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:28/r8.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI:89:28/r8.claim: After a man recited these verses and Abū Bakr praised them, the Prophet told Abū Bakr that an angel would say these words to him.
RAZI:89:28/r8.anchor: أحسن هذا ! فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام
